idiom_name: Codable synthesis: the generated init(from:) asks only for its own CodingKeys (decodeIfPresent(_:forKey:) ?? default for absent keys)
implementation_notes: Swift's compiler-synthesised init(from:) queries a keyed container only for the properties in CodingKeys, so JSONDecoder silently skips every unknown key in the payload - tolerance is the default and additive producer changes cannot break a Codable type. The missing-field half is not synthesised: an optional property becomes nil, while a non-optional one throws unless the reader declares a custom init(from:) using decodeIfPresent(_:forKey:) ?? default (or a property wrapper). Choose the manual initialiser when defaults or presence semantics must be explicit rather than implicit.
pitfalls: Missing keys are only tolerated through optionals or decodeIfPresent; a non-optional property makes the whole payload fail with keyNotFound, and a key that is present but null fails with valueNotFound, which are different failure modes to handle.

Key-name drift is silent in one direction only: a producer rename makes the property absent (default applied) rather than raising, so snake_case payloads need keyDecodingStrategy or explicit CodingKeys raw values.
Codable is tolerant about keys but strict about types - an Int-to-String change still throws - and decodeIfPresent collapses "absent" and "explicit null" into the same nil.
